clue.text: Male stand-in in audition for play

indicators.note: the male pronoun and the stand-in sit inside the audition word

parts.note: an audition is a test of a performer
he is the male pronoun
a temp is a temporary stand-in worker

explanation.surface: A man covering for an absent actor reads at an audition for a play.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Audition' wants to be the homophone signal; instead it is the test that the male temp goes 'in'.
explanation.definitionFit: Shakespeare wrote this late romance, set on Prospero's island, as a stage drama.

clue.text: It's best put on Indian's head

definitions.text: It's best put on Indian's head

indicators.note: in a down entry the top word is placed on the following letter

parts.note: top means best

indicators.note: the head of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: The finest hat is worn by a man from India.
explanation.walkthrough: 'put on' places TOP above the I from 'head' of Indian's; read whole, the clue describes the hat.
explanation.definitionFit: A topi is a light sun helmet worn in India, so it sits on an Indian head.

clue.text: Language of poetry lacking a bit of vitality

indicators.note: the poetry word goes without the letter that follows

parts.note: verse is poetry

indicators.note: a bit of means just the first letter of the next word

explanation.surface: A tongue for poems that lack spark.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a bit of' gives V from vitality; 'lacking' drops it from VERSE.
explanation.definitionFit: Erse is an old name for the Gaelic tongue of Scotland or Ireland.

clue.text: Greek scholar in muse's former quarters

parts.note: Erato is the muse of love poetry
then means at a former time
E and S are compass quarters, east and south

explanation.surface: An ancient academic stays in the rooms where a muse once lived.
explanation.walkthrough: 'quarters' looks like lodgings; here it is two compass points, E and S.
explanation.definitionFit: This ancient Greek polymath measured the Earth's circumference and ran Alexandria's library.

indicators.note: in a down entry the supporting word sits under the other

parts.note: lead means principal, as in the lead role

explanation.surface: The head teacher backs a pupil called Penny in her appeal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'supports' puts LEAD below P in the down entry.
explanation.definitionFit: To plead is to beg or make an earnest request, a verb sense of appeal.

indicators.note: composed means the letters are put together in a new arrangement

explanation.surface: A tune written in the Greek capital, for instance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'composed' rearranges ATHENS and SAY.
explanation.definitionFit: A sea shanty is a work song sung by sailors.

clue.text: Mark appears in A Christmas Carol

indicators.note: the letters appear inside the run of the Dickens title

explanation.surface: A blemish shows up in a copy of the Dickens story.
explanation.walkthrough: 'appears in' signals the run hidden across ChristmaS CARol.
explanation.definitionFit: A scar is the mark left on skin by a healed wound.

indicators.note: varied means the letters of the word are changed around

explanation.surface: Bring together a mix of ornaments.
explanation.walkthrough: 'varied' rearranges DECORATION.
explanation.definitionFit: To coordinate parts is to bring them into harmonious working together.

clue.text: Dad ran riot, oddly enough when slowing down

indicators.note: oddly enough means the letters fall out in an unexpected order

explanation.surface: Father went wild, strangely, while easing off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'oddly enough' rearranges DAD RAN RIOT.
explanation.definitionFit: Ritardando is the musical direction for gradually reducing tempo.

clue.text: Die when embracing Georgia in corridor

indicators.note: the dying phrase wraps its arms round the state abbreviation

parts.note: to pass away is a euphemism for to die
GE is an abbreviation for Georgia

explanation.surface: Someone expires while hugging a Southern belle in a hallway.
explanation.walkthrough: 'embracing' puts GE inside PASS AWAY, between PASS and AWAY.
explanation.definitionFit: A passageway is a narrow way through a building, synonymous with a hallway.

annotationWithheld.why: 'Beast is put down' (4) for GOAT: 'Beast' defines it, but nothing in 'is put down' gives the letters, and no blog for this 2007 puzzle was found; probably an OCR or setter slip

indicators.note: the mocking word grips the other inside it

parts.note: guying means mocking or ridiculing
manner means style

explanation.surface: Ridicule holds a novel's style in its grip.
explanation.walkthrough: 'gripping' marks the container. This is an 1815 Walter Scott novel, little read now, named after its hero.
explanation.definitionFit: Walter Scott published this book in 1815, the second of his Waverley series.

clue.text: Tory ought, in more primitive environment, to ignore

parts.note: C is the abbreviation for Conservative, the Tory party

indicators.note: the more-primitive word forms surroundings for the word for ought

parts.note: older things are more primitive
ought means should

explanation.surface: A Conservative politician thinks we should return to a simpler world, where problems are simply ignored.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in ... environment' is split around 'more primitive', the container; 'Tory' (C) stands in front.
explanation.definitionFit: To cold-shoulder someone is to snub them deliberately, treating them as absent.

clue.text: Hearts' man in place for match record

indicators.note: the hearts and man go inside the place word

parts.note: to set is to place
cores are hearts, the central parts
he is the male pronoun

explanation.surface: A Heart of Midlothian footballer stands in position for a match report.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' marks the container. Hearts is an Edinburgh football club, which suits the surface, but here hearts are simply centres.
explanation.definitionFit: A scoresheet records the points or goals in a game.

indicators.note: the motorway letter sits inside the disrepair word

parts.note: ruination is a state of ruin or disrepair
M is the abbreviation for motorway, as in M1

explanation.surface: Reflections on a crumbling highway.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' marks the container; Britain's motorways are numbered M1, M25 and so on.
explanation.definitionFit: Rumination is deep, prolonged thought or pondering.

indicators.note: a disaster leaves the letters of the words wrecked and rearranged

explanation.surface: A kept woman tells the story of a catastrophe.
explanation.walkthrough: 'disaster' rearranges RECOUNTS and A.
explanation.definitionFit: A courtesan was a paid companion to wealthy men, a kept lover.

clue.text: A pub is not out of the urban sprawl

indicators.note: out means the letters are put out of order

explanation.surface: A suburban pub isn't part of the city's outskirts.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out' rearranges A PUB IS NOT.
explanation.definitionFit: Subtopia is a disparaging name for sprawling suburbs, and this adjective describes them.

parts.note: a guy is a man
ta is British informal for thanks

explanation.surface: A fellow thanks someone named Ray.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ray' looks like a man's name, but it is the fish.
explanation.definitionFit: The manta is a huge ocean ray, a flat cartilaginous fish.

indicators.note: the word for flattery loses its head, its opening letter

parts.note: praise is flattering talk

explanation.surface: Vacuous compliments only overstate things.
explanation.walkthrough: 'empty-headed' drops the first letter of PRAISE.
explanation.definitionFit: To raise something is to increase or inflate it, as when overstating a claim.

parts.note: to bay is to howl like a hound
a means one
Ted is a boy's name

explanation.surface: A dog howls as a lad stands rooted to the spot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'transfixed' seems to mean spellbound; here it is literal, pierced by a blade.
explanation.definitionFit: Transfixed literally means pierced right through, as by a soldier's blade on a rifle.

parts.note: SK is the international code for Slovakia
ate is an old sense of to irritate, as in what's eating you
a boarder is a paying lodger

explanation.surface: An athlete living in Slovakia is annoyed with a lodger.
explanation.walkthrough: 'irritated' gives ATE, past tense of eat in the sense of bother or annoy.
explanation.definitionFit: Riding a board on wheels is a recognised sport, so its rider is a sportsman.

clue.text: Bishop without elevated self awareness is understood

indicators.note: without here means outside, so the bishop letters surround the rest

parts.note: RR is Right Reverend, a bishop's title

indicators.note: elevated in a down entry means the word is read upwards

parts.note: ego is one's sense of self

explanation.surface: A bishop lacking high self-esteem is still understood.
explanation.walkthrough: 'elevated' reverses the self word upwards in this down entry; 'without' in its old sense of outside puts the bishop's two letters round it.
explanation.definitionFit: Roger is radio talk confirming a message was received.

annotationWithheld.why: 'Pack of Bishop's Tipple' (4) for DALE: 'Tipple' gives ALE, but nothing in 'Pack of Bishop's' gives D or a definition of valley; garbled or OCR-damaged and no blog was found

definitions.meaning: a dining hall for service personnel
a stew can be a muddle or confused state

explanation.definitionFit: A military dining room is a mess, and so is a muddle or jam.

indicators.note: sounds signals that the word for mysterious is said aloud

parts.note: eerie means strange and mysterious

explanation.surface: A lake has a spooky quality to it.
explanation.definitionFit: Lake Erie is one of the Great Lakes of North America.

clue.text: Crowd collects ghastly silver in mission

indicators.note: the crowd word gathers the others inside it

parts.note: a pile is a crowd, heap or mass
grim means ghastly
Ag is the chemical symbol for silver

explanation.surface: A mob gathers dreadful silver on a sacred journey.
explanation.walkthrough: 'collects' marks the container, the crowd swallowing both the ghastly word and the silver symbol.
explanation.definitionFit: A pilgrimage is a journey undertaken as a religious duty or quest.

indicators.note: returning means the run of a and the word for stone is read backwards

parts.note: a nut is the hard stone or kernel of a fruit

explanation.surface: Bringing back a heavy weight of fish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Returning' turns A + NUT round. 'Stone' wants to be the weight; it is a kernel.
explanation.definitionFit: Tuna is a large ocean fish of the mackerel family.

clue.text: Maestro going through entrance? That's taking place!

indicators.note: the expert word passes through the middle of the entrance word

parts.note: ingress means an entrance or the act of entering
a pro is an expert, as a maestro is

explanation.surface: A conductor walks through the doorway as the event begins.
explanation.walkthrough: 'going through' marks the container; the question mark flags ingress as a less familiar word for entrance.
explanation.definitionFit: Something in progress is underway, happening now.
